title: An empty answer is not the same as no answer.
hook: An empty answer is not the same as no answer. Most systems pretend they are the same.
thesis: A core PING principle: failure is information. When a retrieval call degrades, the system must say so; it may never return an empty result that quietly means the infrastructure broke. Concretely, vector retrieval that degraded is a different state from a query that genuinely matched nothing, and the two must never look identical to the caller. This post teaches the idea with that one concrete example.

verified: PING's principle: failures have typed semantics; an empty answer is never allowed to hide an infrastructure failure (SOUL.md principle 11, via SYSTEMS.md section 1).
inferred: Silently degraded retrieval is a real source of wrong answers in other systems; naming the principle gives engineers a design rule.
